starting_principles: Definition of moment of inertia for continuous mass distributions: $I = \int r_\perp^2 \, dm$
Definition of center of mass: $\int \vec{r}_{\text{cm}} \, dm = \vec{0}$ in the center-of-mass reference frame
Vector decomposition of position vectors in parallel planes: $\vec{r}_\perp = \vec{r}'_\perp - \vec{d}$
assumptions: The body is a rigid body with invariant mass density distribution.
The two axes of rotation are strictly parallel and separated by a perpendicular distance $d$.
One of the two parallel axes passes through the body's center of mass (CM).

ordered_steps.description: Establish a coordinate frame with origin at the center of mass (CM) and align the $z$-axis with the CM rotation axis.
ordered_steps.operation: Set coordinate system with origin $O$ at the center of mass, taking the rotation axis through CM as the $z$-axis. The parallel axis $z'$ is displaced by a perpendicular vector $\vec{d} = d_x \hat{i} + d_y \hat{j}$ in the $xy$-plane, where $|\vec{d}| = d = \sqrt{d_x^2 + d_y^2}$.
assumptions_applied: One axis passes through the center of mass.
The two rotation axes are parallel.

ordered_steps.description: Express the position of a mass element $dm$ relative to the center of mass and relative to the displaced parallel axis.
ordered_steps.operation: Let the position vector of mass element $dm$ in the CM frame be $\vec{r}' = x' \hat{i} + y' \hat{j} + z' \hat{k}$. Its position vector relative to the parallel axis $z'$ is $\vec{r} = \vec{r}' - \vec{d} = (x' - d_x)\hat{i} + (y' - d_y)\hat{j} + z' \hat{k}$.

ordered_steps.description: Compute the square of the perpendicular distance from the parallel axis $z'$ to the mass element $dm$.
ordered_steps.operation: Calculate the squared magnitude $r_\perp^2 = |\vec{r}_\perp|^2 = (x' - d_x)^2 + (y' - d_y)^2$ and expand the binomial terms.
ordered_steps.result_equation: $$r_\perp^2 = (x'^2 + y'^2) + (d_x^2 + d_y^2) - 2(x' d_x + y' d_y) = r_\perp'^2 + d^2 - 2 \vec{r}'_\perp \cdot \vec{d}$$
assumptions_applied: Euclidean vector geometry in the perpendicular plane.

ordered_steps.description: Integrate the squared perpendicular distance over the entire mass of the rigid body to obtain total moment of inertia.
ordered_steps.operation: Integrate with respect to mass element $dm$ across the entire body volume $V$: $I = \int r_\perp^2 \, dm$.
assumptions_applied: Distance $d$ is constant for all mass elements of the rigid body.

ordered_steps.description: Evaluate the three integral terms using the definitions of $I_{\text{cm}}$, total mass $M$, and the center of mass reference frame.
ordered_steps.operation: Identify: (1) $\int r_\perp'^2 \, dm = I_{\text{cm}}$ by definition of moment of inertia about the CM axis. (2) $\int dm = M$, so $d^2 \int dm = M d^2$. (3) $\int \vec{r}'_\perp \, dm = M \vec{R}_{\text{cm}, \perp}' = \vec{0}$ because the origin was chosen precisely at the center of mass.
ordered_steps.result_equation: $$\int r_\perp'^2 \, dm = I_{\text{cm}},\quad d^2 \int dm = M d^2,\quad \int \vec{r}'_\perp \, dm = \vec{0}$$
assumptions_applied: Center of mass property: $\int \vec{r}' \, dm = \vec{0}$ in the CM frame.

ordered_steps.description: Substitute the evaluated integrals into the expansion to establish the parallel axis theorem.
ordered_steps.operation: Combine terms to arrive at the final algebraic formula.
assumptions_applied: Cross-term vanishes identically due to CM origin.

applicability_conditions: Must be applied between a center-of-mass axis and a parallel axis; cannot be applied directly between two arbitrary non-CM axes without passing through CM.
The two axes must be strictly parallel.
